applications.description:
Legacy per-Application grant list (admin/editor/viewer
short-enum, slice #322 shape). One entry per
(Application × role) grant. An entry may name explicit
namespaces, vClusters (rendered as additional
namespaces with the vCluster prefix), or omit both —
in which case catalyst-api expands the grant against
Application.k8s_namespaces before applying.

EPIC-3 (#1098) UserAccess CRs authored via the
/rbac/assign endpoint use the new tierRoleRef + scopes
fields instead and may omit applications entirely.
Both shapes coexist during EPIC-3 rollout.

app.description:
Application slug as registered in catalyst-api
(e.g. helmwatch, ai-inference).

namespaces.description:
Explicit namespace list for this grant. When
omitted, catalyst-api resolves it from the
Application's k8s_namespaces field before writing
the CR. A `["*"]` entry materializes a
ClusterRoleBinding instead of per-namespace
RoleBindings.

role.description:
One of admin | editor | viewer. The controller
rewrites this to the canonical ClusterRole name
openova:application-<role>.

vClusters.description:
vCluster names — rendered as additional
namespaces using the catalyst convention
`vcluster-<name>`.

providerConfigRef.description:
Retained for backward-compatibility with CRs authored
against the legacy Crossplane Claim shape. Ignored by
the catalyst-useraccess-controller. Most callers leave
this unset.

scopes.description:
Manara DNA label-based scope tags. Each entry is a
`{key, value}` pair from the canonical openova.io
label vocabulary.

Semantics: AND-within (all scopes must match the
target), OR-across UserAccess CRs (any matching CR
grants access). The wildcard scope
`[{key: "*", value: "*"}]` means cluster-wide.

Empty list = cluster-wide (same as wildcard scope).

Authored by the /rbac/assign endpoint and consumed by
the useraccess-controller's label-matching engine at
`core/controllers/internal/labels/`.

key.description:
Label key from the canonical openova.io
vocabulary (e.g. `openova.io/application`,
`openova.io/env-type`, `openova.io/org`). The
wildcard `*` matches any key.

value.description:
Label value (e.g. `wordpress`, `dev`,
`acme-corp`). The wildcard `*` matches any
value.

sovereignRef.description:
Sovereign identifier — a single DNS label (no dots).
Carried as an ops/audit label on the materialized
RoleBindings.

tierRoleRef.description:
Tier ClusterRole this UserAccess targets — one of
`openova:tier-{viewer,developer,operator,admin,owner}`
(the 5 catalog tiers shipped by EPIC-3 (#1098) slice
T1's tier-clusterroles.yaml).

Authored by the find-or-create-role endpoint
(`POST /api/v1/sovereigns/{id}/rbac/assign`, slice A1)
when an operator picks a tier in the multi-grant
editor. The useraccess-controller binds this
ClusterRole on the target via RoleBinding /
ClusterRoleBinding depending on whether scopes
narrow the target to a namespace.

When unset, the legacy `applications[*].role` short
enum (admin/editor/viewer → openova:application-*)
is used. Both fields can co-exist during EPIC-3
rollout — tierRoleRef takes precedence when both set.

user.description:
Identity of the principal receiving access. Either
keycloakSubject (an OIDC `sub` claim, binding a single
user) or keycloakGroups (a list of group names, binding
every member of those groups) or both. The controller
emits one RoleBinding subject per identity.

keycloakGroups.description:
Keycloak group names. Each renders as an additional
RoleBinding subject of kind=Group,
name="oidc:<group>" (matches --oidc-groups-prefix).

keycloakSubject.description:
OIDC `sub` claim — the Keycloak user's stable id.
Renders as a RoleBinding subject of kind=User,
name="oidc:<subject>" (matches the api-server
--oidc-username-prefix convention).

phase.description:
Pending → Active on first successful reconcile; Failed
on a hard error. Surfaced to the access-matrix UI.

rolebindingsCreated.description:
Count of RoleBinding / ClusterRoleBinding objects this
UserAccess owns. Surfaced to the user-access editor
UI's "<n> grants active" badge.

apps.openova.io/v1/Application.description:
Application is an installed instance of a Blueprint, owned by an
Organization, deployed into one or more regions per its Placement,
managed by Flux.

One Application = one Gitea repo at
gitea.{location-code}.{sovereign-domain}/{org}/{app}; branches
develop/staging/main map to dev/stg/prod Environments.

See docs/EPICS-1-6-unified-design.md §3.2.3 and
docs/BLUEPRINT-AUTHORING.md §3 for the contract.

version.description: Semver of the Blueprint OCI artifact.

bootstrap.description:
True for bootstrap-owned instances: slot-installed
HelmReleases whose chart self-registers this
Application CR as the canonical representation
(#3370). The application-controller ADOPTS such an
instance — it skips every render / fan-out / Gitea
path (the install is already owned by the
bootstrap-kit HR; rendering would duplicate it) and
only reconciles status by observing
spec.helmRelease's Ready condition.

dependsOn.description:
Backing-service wiring (#3370). Each entry names
another Application (the backing instance) this
Application consumes, optionally with the Context it
occupies on that instance. The
application-controller resolves each entry to the
backing instance's HelmRelease(s) and stamps Flux
`spec.dependsOn` on every HR it renders — the
runtime wiring is purely Flux, no controller magic.

context.description:
The Context this Application occupies on the
backing instance, as `<kind>/<name>` (e.g.
`db/gitea`). Display + provenance only — the
Flux wiring uses the resolved HelmRelease.

namespace.description:
Backing Application namespace. Defaults to
this Application's own namespace.

environmentRef.description:
Name of the Environment CR (e.g. acme-prod) this Application
belongs to. Environment determines vCluster targets and
Gitea branch.

path.description: HTTP(S) path probed for liveness from outside the cluster.

port.description: Service port name or numeric port.

helmRelease.description:
The owning Flux HelmRelease of a bootstrap-owned
instance (spec.bootstrap=true). The controller's
adoption path observes its Ready condition for
status; console projections dedupe HR-derived rows
against it.

instanceId.description:
Stable per-instance identifier. Immutable after
creation — the admission webhook rejects any update
that changes it. Defaults to the first 8 chars of
metadata.uid when unset.

isolationLevel.description:
`namespace` (default) — every Application instance
is a distinct Namespace within the Org's host
cluster(s); HelmReleases target that namespace.
`vcluster` — instances land inside the Org's
existing vCluster (one vCluster per Org per host
cluster); HR names differ via namingTemplate, the
namespace inside the vCluster is shared. New
isolation modes require an ADR.

namingTemplate.description:
Go-template syntax. Default depends on
isolationLevel: `{{.AppName}}-{{.InstanceID}}` for
`namespace`, `{{.AppName}}` for `vcluster`. Template
context: `.AppName` (metadata.name), `.InstanceID`
(spec.instanceId), `.OrgSlug` (label
catalyst.openova.io/organization), `.Blueprint`
(blueprintRef.name without `bp-` prefix).

owners.description: Per-Application owner list. Roles materialize as UserAccess via useraccess-controller.

parameters.description:
User-supplied values, validated against the Blueprint's
spec.configSchema (BLUEPRINT-AUTHORING.md §3-§4).
Free-form here; the application-controller and the
blueprint-controller's admission webhook enforce the
schema match at admission.

placement.description:
Placement of this instance (#3969): an OBJECT
{mode, targets, ownedDependencies, regions, clusters,
vcluster}. `mode` is the posture (singleton = one cluster
only; active-active = manifests fan out to all regions[];
active-hot-standby / active-passive = primary in
regions[0], standby in regions[1..]; failover managed by
the Continuum controller); `targets[]` is the per-target
desired state the pattern is derived from. Defaulted from
the Blueprint's defaultPlacement; gated by its
allowedPlacements + placementCapability. The bare posture
STRING is the legacy spelling: accepted on read and
migrated to {mode} by the application-controller.

regions.description:
Host clusters this Application targets, in priority order.
For active-hotstandby, regions[0] is the primary.

topology.description: DR / scaling knobs read by the Continuum controller (#1101).

minReplicas.description: Lower bound for any HPA the Blueprint declares.

x-kubernetes-validations.message: spec.environmentRef and spec.regions are required unless spec.bootstrap=true (bootstrap-owned instance)

activity.description:
ADR-0015 D7/D8 — structured activity of an in-flight
topology transition (one entry per phase × member).
Projected verbatim into Jobs as type
`topology-transition`. Populated by the D8 transition
engine; empty otherwise.

transition.description: The transition record id this entry belongs to (one Jobs record per move; Refs

giteaRepo.description: Full URL of the per-Application Gitea repo (e.g. gitea.hfmp.omantel.openova.io/acme/marketing-site).

installedBlueprint.description: Snapshot of the Blueprint actually rendered (post upgrade-resolve).

placement.description:
#3373 — the EFFECTIVE placement the last reconcile
resolved + rendered (instance > Blueprint default >
legacy seams). The console reflects this — it mirrors
the Git-committed truth, never fights it.

#4601 — additionally carries the EFFECTIVE per-region DR
split ({mode, primaryRegion, standbyRegions,
replicationLagSeconds, leaseHeld}) so the per-app Topology
DR strip can render primary↔standby. The primary is the
LIVE Continuum leaseHolder when a per-app Continuum exists
(so the projection tracks failover, not just config),
else the configured plan primary (regions[0]). Read-only /
observational — REPORTS placement, never changes it.

leaseHeld.description:
The per-app Continuum's LeaseHeld condition (omitted
when no Continuum exists).

mode.description:
Resolved canonical placement mode (singleton |
active-active | active-hot-standby | active-passive).

primaryRegion.description:
Effective primary region — the LIVE Continuum
leaseHolder when a per-app Continuum exists, else the
configured plan primary (regions[0]). Empty for
active-active (no primary concept).

replicationLagSeconds.description:
Replication lag from the per-app Continuum status
(omitted when no Continuum reported one).

source.description:
Which declaration won the resolution: instance |
blueprint-default | blueprint-placementSchema |
host-default.

standbyRegions.description:
Every plan region except the effective primary, in
plan (priority) order. After a failover the OLD
primary appears here.

primaryRegion.description: Currently-primary host cluster. Switched by the Continuum controller on failover.

conditions.description:
ADR-0015 D7 — per-region conditions. Carries the
region's `Serving` condition (functional probe:
the route answers through the region's gateway;
a CNPG primary with required synchronous
replication has its synchronous standby).
Unknown when the region is not observable from
the controller instance that wrote it.

catalyst.openova.io/v1/Blueprint.description:
Blueprint is the unified unit of installable software. See
docs/BLUEPRINT-AUTHORING.md §3 for the contract.

Schema is intentionally permissive (x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields
on free-form sub-trees: configSchema, manifests.values, depends[].values,
and the spec root) because:
  - configSchema is per-Blueprint JSON Schema — its shape is
    arbitrary by design.
  - 58 existing blueprint.yaml files (38 v1alpha1 + 20 v1) carry
    a union of card variants (summary|description, category|family,
    docs|documentation), optional manifests blocks for catalog-
    metadata-only entries, and one-off fields (outputs, etc.).
  - Tightening happens via follow-up slices that author specific
    ClusterPolicies or schema bumps.

Required at this layer: spec.version, spec.card.title. Everything
else is optional / preserve-unknown.

allowedPlacements.description:
#3373 — vCluster tiers an instance of this Blueprint MAY
be placed in. Empty/absent = unrestricted. The
application-controller fails an Application whose
effective vcluster is not in this list; the console's
generic advanced selector renders its options from it.

configSchema.description:
Per-Blueprint JSON Schema that drives the install form
in the console. Free-form by design — preserve-unknown.

consoleUI.description:
Wave 5.69 (#2370) — Sovereign-console UI registration
contract for third-party Blueprints (bp-agenity is
the first consumer; see docs/INTEGRATION-OPENOVA-MCP.md
§5). When sidebarEntry=true the SovereignSidebar.tsx
appends a nav entry between the hardcoded last entry
(BSS) and Settings, in sidebarOrder order. RBAC is
inherited from existing tier-gate.

sidebarEntry.description: When true, register a top-level Sovereign-console sidebar nav entry.

sidebarIcon.description:
SVG path string for the icon (single-stroke, Tabler-style;
see existing FLAT_NAV entries in SovereignSidebar.tsx for
the conventional shape). Default uses the blueprint card
icon.

sidebarOrder.description:
Insert-order between BSS (last hardcoded, order=60) and Settings
(order=99 pinned). Higher = closer to Settings. Default 50.

sidebarRoute.description: Route path the nav link navigates to (e.g. /apps/bp-agenity/dashboard).

defaultPlacement.description:
#3373 — the placement every instance of this Blueprint
inherits unless its own Application.spec.placement
overrides a field. Mirrors the object form of
Application.spec.placement.

endpoints.description:
Named external endpoints surfaced by this Blueprint.
The Endpoints tab UI (G117.3) renders one card per
entry; the Launch button UI (G117.4) starts from
launchDefault=true (else first ssoEnabled https).

healthPath.description:
ADR-0015 D7 — path the application-controller's
per-region Serving probe GETs through the region's
gateway (Host = the route hostname). Any response
< 500 means the endpoint is serving. Default "/".

hostnameTemplate.description:
Go text/template emitting an RFC-1123 hostname
after evaluation.

Tokens the resolver ACTUALLY implements
(catalyst-api resolveHostnameTemplate):
{{.SovereignFQDN}} {{.OrgSlug}} {{.AppName}}
{{.OrgDomain}}.

{{.OrgDomain}} (#5389) is the Organization's own
domain suffix — <subdomain>.<tenantPublic.parentDomain>
for a pool Org, falling back to
<slug>.<SovereignFQDN> for a single-domain Org. It is
the ONLY correct way to name a per-Org app host: live
per-Org HTTPRoutes are served on the pool domain
(agenity.uatco.omani.homes), never on
<app>.<org>.<SovereignFQDN>. Composing {{.OrgSlug}}
with {{.SovereignFQDN}} yields a host with no
HTTPRoute, no DNS and no certificate.

{{.InstanceID}} and {{.ClusterID}} were documented
here but were NEVER implemented by the resolver. Since
#5389 an unimplemented token is a hard resolution
FAILURE: the endpoint reports status Unresolved with
no hostname and no launchURL, rather than emitting a
URL with the literal braces still in it.

x-kubernetes-validations.message: endpoints[].hostnameTemplate references {{.InstanceID}} or {{.ClusterID}}, which the resolver has never implemented — it substitutes only SovereignFQDN, OrgSlug, AppName and OrgDomain. For a per-instance host use {{.AppName}}: multiInstance.namingTemplate already makes the Application CR name instance-unique.

ssoInitPath.description:
App-local OIDC-init route the console "Open"
launch lands the browser on (e.g. Grafana
`/login/generic_oauth`, Harbor `/c/oidc/login`),
which 302s to Keycloak with the app's pre-baked
kc_idp_hint for silent SSO. Empty/absent →
legacy app-root launch. (#3150)

hasUserUIEndpoint.description:
True when this Blueprint exposes a user-facing UI front
door (drives the console AppCard's "Open…" placeholder).
Defaults from spec.endpoints[] (ssoEnabled / launchDefault
/ name="ui") when omitted.

helmRelease.description:
Flux HelmRelease install/upgrade behaviour the
application-controller stamps on the rendered HR (#4246).

disableWait.description:
Stamp install.disableWait + upgrade.disableWait on the
rendered HelmRelease so helm-controller does NOT block on
workload readiness before running post-install/post-upgrade
hooks. Required by charts whose Pod gates on a value one of
the chart's own post-install hooks populates (e.g. bp-newapi
DSN-gate). Default false.

multiInstance.description:
When enabled, a Blueprint may have >1 Application
instance per Organization. Catalog cards show the
instance-count badge + "+ New instance" button.
When absent / enabled=false, a Blueprint is
singleton-per-Org.

producesInstances.description:
#3648 — declares this Blueprint is an OPERATOR/engine
that PRODUCES shareable data-instances of another
(instance) Blueprint. The DECLARED, app-agnostic
replacement for hardcoded "postgres operator"
knowledge: any operator Blueprint that sets this gets
the engine-class-card / instance-creation treatment and
the backing-service generator resolves a consumer's
`backingServices[].type: <kind>` to
`<instanceBlueprint>-<instance>` — no engine-name
literal in the platform engine.

instanceBlueprint.description:
The instance Blueprint id this operator provisions
(e.g. `bp-postgres`); the dependsOn HR prefix.

kind.description:
The engine-class id the instances are OF (e.g.
`postgres`) — the value a consumer Blueprint names
in backingServices[].type.

sso.description:
Blueprint-level SSO declaration. Tier-1/2 use realm
`sovereign`; Tier-3 use per-Org realm via
`{{.OrgSlug}}` template token.

adminGroup.description:
#3648 — the STANDARD, app-agnostic Sovereign-realm
GROUP whose members are elevated to the app's admin
role. Every Blueprint that needs a first admin
seeded via the Sovereign SSO names the group HERE
instead of in a chart-bespoke values key. Elevation
always keys on the group, never a per-user identity
(#3374 §5). Default `sovereign-admins`.

bootstrap.description:
#3648 — the STANDARD sso-bootstrap stanza: when set,
the platform seeds the app's FIRST admin via the
Sovereign SSO (Pattern B — apps with no group→role
config knob, honoured by the chart's own seeding
mechanism, never keyed on the app name in the
engine).

topology.description:
Per-Blueprint multi-region declaration. Admission
enforces defaults.multi-region + defaults.single-region
are members of supported, and every key in perTopology
is in supported.

perTopology.description:
Per-variant replication / switchover / placement
knobs. Each variant repeats the same three
sub-schemas — K8s structural CRD schemas forbid
$ref so each variant is inlined via YAML anchor.

x-kubernetes-validations.message: topology.defaults.multi-region must be a member of topology.supported[]
topology.defaults.single-region must be a member of topology.supported[]

ociDigest.description: cosign-signed OCI artifact digest (set by CI on publish).

catalyst.openova.io/v1/Environment.description:
Environment is the user-facing scope where Applications are
installed. Logical concept: one Environment can be realized by
N vClusters across regions × building blocks.

Naming: spec.organizationRef + spec.envType compose the
Environment name `{org}-{envType}` per NAMING-CONVENTION.md
§11. Examples: acme-prod, acmebank-uat.

DR is a Placement on the *Application*, not an Env Type — there
is no `*-dr` Environment. Multi-region disaster-recovery
topology lives on Application.spec.placement.

See docs/EPICS-1-6-unified-design.md §3.2.2 and
docs/NAMING-CONVENTION.md §11.

envType.description:
Per NAMING §2.4. The full Env name is composed as
{organizationRef}-{envType} (e.g. acme-prod). DR is
NOT an envType — see Application.spec.placement.

organizationRef.description: Slug of the parent Organization CR.

placement.description:
single-region = exactly 1 region in regions[].
multi-region = 2+ regions, vClusters realized in each.

policyRef.description:
Optional name of an EnvironmentPolicy CR that gates
promotion (approvers, soak duration) and configures
compliance weights for this Environment.

hostCluster.description:
Optional explicit host-cluster name override. If empty,
environment-controller derives {provider}-{region}-{buildingBlock}-{envType}.

giteaRepoRef.description:
Per Naming §11.2 each Application gets its own Gitea
repo; the Environment maps to a *branch* across those
repos (develop/staging/main ↔ dev/stg/prod).

jetstreamSubjectPrefix.description:
Per ARCHITECTURE.md §5 + NAMING §11.2 item 4, the
JetStream subject prefix for this Environment is
ws.{organizationRef}-{envType}.>

regionCount.description: Number of regions in spec.regions[] — convenient printer column.

catalyst.openova.io/v1/EnvironmentPolicy.description:
EnvironmentPolicy gates promotion (approvers + soak duration)
and configures compliance scoring (per-policy weight + mode
permissive|enforcing) for a given Environment.

Referenced by Environment.spec.policyRef. Consumed by:
- environment-controller for promotion gating (slice C2)
- compliance-aggregator for weighted score rollups (#1096)
- Kyverno policy renderer (#1096) — `mode` flips between
  `validationFailureAction: Audit` (permissive) and `Enforce`

See docs/EPICS-1-6-unified-design.md §3.2.5 and §4 (EPIC-1).

modes.description:
Policy name → mode (permissive|enforcing). Permissive
= audit-only (Kyverno validationFailureAction=Audit).
Enforcing = blocks at admission (=Enforce).

scope.description:
Restrict this policy to a workload class.
Compliance-aggregator treats unset as 'all'.

weights.description:
Policy name → weight config. Each entry carries
a numeric weight (0-100) and an optional scope
(stateful|stateless|all — default 'all' applied
by the compliance-aggregator at read time, not
by the schema, per K8s structural-schema rules).
Sum is normalized across applicable policies;
scope=stateful entries are dropped from the
denominator on stateless workloads.

promotion.description: Promotion gates between Environments (e.g. dev → prod).

requiredApprovers.description:
Number of distinct human approvers required to
promote into THIS Environment from a lower
env_type. 0 = automatic.

requiredComplianceScore.description:
Optional compliance-score floor. If set, the
candidate Application's score in the lower
Environment must meet or exceed this value before
promotion. Tied to spec.compliance.weights.

soakHours.description:
Required time the candidate version must have run
in the lower env_type before promotion. 0 = no soak.

appliedAt.description: When environment-controller last reconciled this policy onto its Environments.

policyCount.description: Number of compliance policies declared in spec.compliance.weights.

When absent / enabled=false, a Blueprint is

producesInstances.description:
#3648 — declares this Blueprint is an OPERATOR/engine
that PRODUCES shareable data-instances of another
(instance) Blueprint. The DECLARED, app-agnostic
replacement for hardcoded "postgres operator"
knowledge: any operator Blueprint that sets this gets
the engine-class-card / instance-creation treatment and
the backing-service generator resolves a consumer's
`backingServices[].type: <kind>` to
`<instanceBlueprint>-<instance>` — no engine-name
literal in the platform engine.

instanceBlueprint.description:
The instance Blueprint id this operator provisions
(e.g. `bp-postgres`); the dependsOn HR prefix.

kind.description:
The engine-class id the instances are OF (e.g.
`postgres`) — the value a consumer Blueprint names
in backingServices[].type.

sso.description:
Blueprint-level SSO declaration. Tier-1/2 use realm
`sovereign`; Tier-3 use per-Org realm via
`{{.OrgSlug}}` template token.

adminGroup.description:
#3648 — the STANDARD, app-agnostic Sovereign-realm
GROUP whose members are elevated to the app's admin
role. Every Blueprint that needs a first admin
seeded via the Sovereign SSO names the group HERE
instead of in a chart-bespoke values key. Elevation
always keys on the group, never a per-user identity
(#3374 §5). Default `sovereign-admins`.

bootstrap.description:
#3648 — the STANDARD sso-bootstrap stanza: when set,
the platform seeds the app's FIRST admin via the
Sovereign SSO (Pattern B — apps with no group→role
config knob, honoured by the chart's own seeding
mechanism, never keyed on the app name in the
engine).

topology.description:
Per-Blueprint multi-region declaration. Admission
enforces defaults.multi-region + defaults.single-region
are members of supported, and every key in perTopology
is in supported.

perTopology.description:
Per-variant replication / switchover / placement
knobs. Each variant repeats the same three
sub-schemas — K8s structural CRD schemas forbid
$ref so each variant is inlined via YAML anchor.

x-kubernetes-validations.message: topology.defaults.multi-region must be a member of topology.supported[]
topology.defaults.single-region must be a member of topology.supported[]

ociDigest.description: cosign-signed OCI artifact digest (set by CI on publish).

catalyst.openova.io/v1alpha1/Sovereign.description:
Sovereign is the K8s-native record of a Catalyst Sovereign — one
deployed Catalyst instance (mothership or franchised). The CR is
the canonical truth-source for: (a) the per-Sovereign FQDN that
console / api / marketplace bind to; (b) the multi-region
topology (regions[]) that catalyst-api's chooseTopology consults
via `Handler.detectMultiRegion` (locked decision #7,
`len(Sovereign.spec.regions) > 1` = multi-region); (c) the
bcpTopology declaration that pillar 3 (zero-tx-loss) gates on;
(d) the parent-domain pool used by per-Org tenant subdomains;
(e) the operator-issued deploymentId used to correlate the
tofu workdir on the catalyst-api PVC.

One Sovereign CR per cluster, cluster-scoped, name conventionally
matches the FQDN's leftmost label or `sovereign-self` for the
local Sovereign. The CR is created by bp-self-sovereign-cutover
step-01 on franchised Sovereigns, and by the mothership
bootstrap on the OpenOva Sovereign.

Closes Gap 5 of #2856: prior to this CRD, `kubectl get sovereign`
returned "no resources" on every Sovereign and catalyst-api's
CountSovereignRegions silently fell through to the
SOVEREIGN_REGIONS env var (also unset), defeating multi-region
endpoint selection.

Refs #2856 #2742 #2737.

bcpTopology.description:
Business-Continuity-Planning topology the operator
selected at signup. `single-region` is one region (no
BCP, dev/preview only). `active-hotstandby` is the
default for production — primary region serves traffic,
standby is warm, failover via Continuum. `active-active`
is multi-master (CNPG quorum split, all regions serve).
Both BCP variants require `len(regions)>=2` per Pillar 3.

deploymentId.description:
16-char hex correlation id for the per-Sovereign tofu
workdir on the catalyst-api `catalyst-api-deployments`
PVC (`/deps/tofu/<deployment-id>/`). Stable for the life
of the Sovereign; immutable after creation.

fqdn.description:
Canonical Sovereign FQDN (e.g. `omantel.omani.works`,
`t38.omani.works`). Hosts console.<fqdn>, api.<fqdn>,
marketplace.<fqdn>, and every per-Org tenant subdomain.
Lowercase, RFC-1123 hostname pattern with at least one
dot (no bare labels).

parentDomains.description:
Pool of registered DNS domains the Sovereign-side
PowerDNS is authoritative for. Exactly one entry MUST
carry `role=primary` (the entry that hosts
console/api/marketplace — matches `spec.fqdn`'s
registered apex). Zero-or-more entries may carry
`role=org-pool` (offered to Organization tenants for free
subdomains). Mirrors the wire shape provisioner.go
ParentDomain emits.

provider.description:
Sovereign-wide default CloudProvider adapter name. Used
as the fallback for `regions[].provider` and as the
dispatch target for `bp-self-sovereign-cutover`.

regions.description:
Per-region declaration in operator-supplied order. The
catalyst-api `Handler.detectMultiRegion` reads
`len(regions)>1` to flip multi-region topology gates;
application-controller's TopologyResolver consults this
list to default `placementSchema.defaultOnMultiRegion`.

Index 0 is conventionally the primary; downstream
consumers must not rely on that ordering for promotion
(use Continuum / status.regions for live state).

az.description:
Optional cloud-provider availability-zone tag.
Most providers infer the AZ from `code`; pass
explicit `az` only when a single region exposes
multiple physically-distinct AZs (HCS
`me-east-215` exposes `-a` / `-b` / `-c`).

code.description:
Provider-native region code (e.g. `fsn1`,
`hel1`, `me-east-215-a`). Used by the OpenTofu
modules and by the application-controller's
per-region HelmRelease fan-out.

provider.description:
CloudProvider adapter name (hetzner / huawei /
aws / gcp / azure / oci). Defaults to the
Sovereign-wide `spec.provider` when absent on a
per-region entry.

role.description:
Operator-meaningful tag for the region's role in
the BCP topology. Free-form; common values
`primary` (index 0 default), `standby`,
`active` (active-active topology).

conditions.description:
Standard k8s conditions[] (type/status/reason/message/
lastTransitionTime). Reconcilers append; readers
consume via meta.IsStatusConditionTrue.

ready.description:
True once the Sovereign has completed bootstrap and
every declared region has reconciled at least once.

regionCount.description:
Materialised count of regions actually reconciled —
mirrors `len(status.regions)`. Used by Console
printer-columns for at-a-glance topology check.

regions.description:
Per-region materialised state — populated from the
provisioner's `MaterializedRegions[]` slice and refreshed
on every reconcile. May lag `spec.regions[]` while a
fresh region rolls.

kubeconfigPath.description:
On-disk path to the per-region kubeconfig under
`catalyst-api-deployments` PVC
(`/deps/kubeconfigs/<id>-<region>-<i>.yaml`).
Surface for the chroot fallback path documented
in feedback_chroot_in_cluster_fallback.md.

dr.openova.io/v1/CNPGPair.description:
CNPGPair binds a CloudNative-PG primary Cluster CR + a replica
Cluster CR across two regions for the Continuum DR loop.

Per ADR-0001 §2.7 + docs/MULTI-REGION-DNS.md the Continuum
controller observes the CNPGPair status to decide when a
switchover is safe (replica is `streaming` AND walLagSeconds
≤ rpoSeconds). The cnpg-pair-controller (Phase-2) reconciles
the underlying postgresql.cnpg.io Cluster CRs and writes
status here.

primaryCluster.description: Name of the primary postgresql.cnpg.io Cluster CR.

replicaCluster.description: Name of the replica postgresql.cnpg.io Cluster CR.

streaming.description: True iff replica is in streaming WAL replication.

walLagSeconds.description: Lag between primary and replica in WAL bytes-time.

dr.openova.io/v1/Continuum.description:
Continuum is the topology-transition contract of one Application
placed across regions (ADR-0015 D8). It is DELIVERED FROM GIT: the
application-controller renders it into the Application's file of
every region (regions/<region-id>/apps/<app>.yaml of the Org repo)
from Application.spec.placement, and every region's Flux applies
it, so the Continuum running in every region reads the same
desired primary.

Changing the Primary is a topology transition: Continuum commits
ordered phases to the region files (traffic-off in the old
primary, data-primary with the CNPG demotion token in the new one,
peers, traffic-on) and waits on the native status of each (CNPG
demotionToken / lastPromotionToken, HelmRelease Ready, the
Application's Serving condition). It writes no workload object.

This CRD is shipped identically by bp-catalyst-platform and
bp-continuum (so a region without the platform umbrella still has
it); scripts/check-continuum-crd-lockstep.sh keeps the two equal.

applicationRef.description: <namespace>/<name> of the Application this Continuum governs.

desiredPrimaryRegion.description:
DESIRED STATE — the region Application.spec.placement
declares Primary, rendered by the application-controller.
Continuum converges the region files onto it.

regions.description: Every region of the placement (canonical region ids), in placement order.

transition.description: Where the region files live and how a transition behaves.

app.description: Application name — the region file key.

autoPromoteOnRegionLoss.description:
When the primary's region is unreachable beyond
regionLossSeconds, commit the move to a surviving
region WITHOUT a demotion token. Default false: a lost
region is reported and nothing is committed.

dependsOn.description:
Continuums ([<namespace>/]<name>) of the Applications
this one consumes (from Application.spec.dependsOn).
A group moves together: traffic stops top-down, state
moves bottom-up, traffic is restored last.

helmRelease.description:
The HelmRelease to observe when it is not rendered by
the application-controller — a bootstrap-kit slot's
HelmRelease, which reads the region file's topology
values ConfigMap through valuesFrom.

repo.description:
The repo holding the region files and the lease:
<path>/regions/<region-id>/<folder>/<app>.yaml and
<path>/continuum/transitions/<group>.yaml. An Org
Application uses its Org repo (path "", folder apps);
a platform Application (installed by a bootstrap-kit
slot) uses the Sovereign region repo
openova/sovereign-regions (path clusters/<fqdn>,
folder platform).

folder.description: Per-region folder of the Application files ("" = apps).

path.description: Folder the region files and the lease live under ("" = repository root).

stateful.description:
The Application carries a CNPG distributed-topology
member per region; traffic-off waits for
status.demotionToken and data-primary commits it as
database.topology.promotionToken.

activity.description:
ADR-0015 D7/D8 — this member's phases of the group's
transition (one entry per phase). Projected verbatim into
Jobs as type `topology-transition`.

transition.description: The transition record id this entry belongs to (one Jobs record per move; Refs

desiredPrimaryRegion.description: The desired primary read from the region files.

leaseHolder.description: Region currently holding the group's Git lease ("" = no transition running).

primaryRegion.description: The primary every region file currently names (Git).

transition.description: The group's current or last transition record (mirrored from Git).

dr.openova.io/v1/PDM.description:
PDM (PowerDNS Manager) — one of N PowerDNS instances that
collectively serve the DNS-quorum lease witness for Continuum
DR. Per ADR-0001 §2.7 + docs/MULTI-REGION-DNS.md the DNS-quorum
lease witness REQUIRES 3 instances minimum (2-of-3 vote);
production sovereigns deploy pdm-1, pdm-2, pdm-3 across host
clusters.

Each PDM CR represents one PowerDNS instance. The continuum-
controller reads the PDM list to discover witnesses and
writes lease TXT records via the PDM API endpoint declared
in spec.endpoint. The PDM controller (cmd/pdm) reconciles
zone state and surfaces health on status.phase.

endpoint.description:
PDM API base URL (e.g. https://pdm-1.openova.io:8081).
Used by continuum-controller to write lease TXT records
via /api/v1/zones/{zone}/rrsets.

region.description: Host-cluster region this PDM lives in.

zone.description:
Default zone this PDM is authoritative for. May be
overridden by per-Continuum spec.pdmZone.

orgs.openova.io/v1/Organization.description:
Organization is the multi-tenant unit on a Sovereign. Per
ADR-0001 §2.7, an Organization is a namespace + a vCluster +
a Keycloak group; this CRD is the K8s-native parent of those
three artifacts plus billing/identity attributes.

Customer Orgs (kind=customer) and internal-team Orgs
(kind=internal) share the SAME shape and the SAME code path.
Difference is the billingMode dimension only.

See docs/EPICS-1-6-unified-design.md §3.2.1 and
docs/NAMING-CONVENTION.md §1.5, §2.5, §4.6.

billingMode.description:
real = invoiced (kind=customer only). chargeback = cost
allocated to internal cost-center. showback = visibility
only, no invoicing.

commerce.description:
Optional record of the marketplace purchase this
Organization was created from (#6971 item 8). The
billing order is the source; core/services/tenant
carries it on `tenant.created`; the provisioning
consumer stamps it here; the chargeback OpenOva
adapter (PROFILE=sovereign) reads it to attach the
Organization's platform Source to its package and
add-on lines. Absent when the Organization was not
created from an order (the sovereign-admin door, or
any Organization that predates the field). The
organization-controller does not reconcile it. No
new entity type — these are optional fields on the
Organization.

addons.description:
BSS add-on SKUs bought with the package, e.g.
"addon.backup". BSS SKUs only — the emitters
filter out the catalog add-on ids the storefront
mixes into the same cart list, so every entry
here attaches to a BSS add-on line directly.

growCeiling.description:
The most a "grow" package may reach. Absent (or a
zero field) = the XL shape: 8 vCPU / 16 GB / 250 GB
disk / 1000 Mbps (twice it on XL). Each value is >=
the package headline; the organization-controller
clamps vcpu and memoryGB (host plan-quota limits)
and diskGB (the in-vCluster app-storage quota) to
[package headline, that ceiling]. bandwidthMbps is
read by BSS only — no bandwidth cap renders.

orderID.description:
The billing order row (core/services/billing
`orders.id`) this Organization was launched from
— the provenance link back to the source.

overageMode.description:
What the package does when usage passes its
headline. "capped" (the default when absent): the
ResourceQuota limits are the package headline.
"grow": the limits are raised to growCeiling and
usage above the headline is billed in arrears by
BSS. The requests side (the guaranteed share) is
the same in both. The organization-controller
reads this to size the ResourceQuota.

packageSKU.description:
BSS package sku the customer chose on the S/M/L/XL
comparison table, e.g. "plan.m". spec.planSlug
stays the catalog plan slug that sizes the
boundary; this is the commercial package it maps
to.

prepaidAmount.description:
OMR the checkout collected for the package and its
BSS add-ons, as a money string ("4.490"). BSS
credits it on the Organization's first statement so
the first period is never charged twice.

priceSource.description:
Where the order's prices came from: "catalog"
(core/services/catalog plan + add-on prices) or
"bss:<price_book>@<prices_as_of>" (the Catalyst
BSS public packages document).

spendLimitMonth.description:
OMR per month the customer allows the overage to
reach, as a money string ("25.000"). Stored and
published here; read and enforced by BSS, which
stamps spec.overageStoppedUntil when it is reached.

costSources.description:
GitOps-declared external cost sources synced into the
chargeback application (ADR-0014 D2). Optional; empty
means the Organization is metered by the platform
collector alone. Each entry names one external cloud
project whose usage the chargeback application
(products/chargeback, EPIC #6723) meters and attributes
to this Organization's app-internal Customer row. The
chargeback OpenOva adapter (PROFILE=sovereign) watches
Organizations and upserts one cost_source per entry.
The project's read-only credential is entered in the
chargeback application; the Organization never names
one. The organization-controller itself does not
reconcile this field.

kind.description:
Cost-source kind. Today only huawei-project
(HCSO Kom4DC); further kinds extend the enum.

projectId.description:
Cloud project id whose usage is metered and
attributed to this Organization.

region.description: Cloud region of the project (e.g. me-east-215).

defaultEnvironmentType.description: Default env_type for new Environments unless overridden.

identity.description:
Federation config — empty means use the Sovereign's own
Keycloak realm. Set to federate Azure SSO / Okta / generic
OIDC into this Org's vCluster.

Slice F2 (#1098) extended `federationConfig` with the
OIDC discovery endpoints + claim-mapper table needed
by the Keycloak IdP CRUD path. The minimum set for a
working Azure-AD federation is: `federationProvider:
azure-sso`, `federationConfig.tenantId`,
`federationConfig.clientId`,
`federationConfig.clientSecretRef`,
`federationConfig.authorizationUrl/tokenUrl/jwksUrl`.
`claimMappers` is OPTIONAL — without it Keycloak's
default `oidc-user-attribute-idp-mapper` for `email`
/ `name` / `given_name` still fires.

claimMappers.description:
Upstream-IdP-claim → Catalyst-user-attribute
mapping table. Each row materializes as one
Keycloak IdentityProviderMapper of type
`oidc-user-attribute-idp-mapper` with
syncMode=INHERIT.

clientSecretRef.description:
Reference to a SealedSecret that holds the OIDC
client secret. Plaintext NEVER on the CR.

#4471: `required: [name, key]` and `key.default`
were REMOVED. `identity.federationConfig` is an
OPTIONAL block ("empty means use the Sovereign's
own realm"), but the controller's Go types model it
as a VALUE struct (orgapi.OrganizationIdentity,
not a pointer) — `,omitempty` is a no-op on a
struct, so on EVERY `client.Update` (e.g. the
tenant-networking finalizer add) the apiserver
receives `clientSecretRef: {}`. With `required`
present + `key` defaulted-in, that empty object
failed validation (`clientSecretRef.name: Required
value`) and wedged ALL reconciles before any
per-Org boundary was produced. Dropping the
required-enforcement here lets an absent federation
round-trip; a configured federation still needs
both name+key, which the controller validates at
readClientSecret() time (organization_controller.go
~L1118) and surfaces on the IdentityProviderConfigured
condition.

jwksUrl.description:
OIDC `jwks_uri`. Keycloak validates ID-token
signatures against the JWKs published here.

tenantId.description:
Azure-AD tenant UUID (or equivalent for other
IdPs). Empty for generic OIDC. Surfaced solely
as a tag on the rendered Keycloak Config map
for operator-debug; Keycloak itself derives
the tenant from the discovery URLs.

kind.description:
customer = external-customer Organization (real billing
or showback). internal = internal-team / department
(chargeback or showback only).

overageStopReason.description: Why grow is held at the headline; empty when it is not.

overageStoppedUntil.description:
BSS spend limit reached (products/chargeback DESIGN.md
§22.11): the grow Organization is held at its package
headline (capped — the host plan-quota limits and the
in-vCluster app-storage quota) until this instant, the
next billing-period start (RFC3339 UTC). Set by the
sovereign-admin API's ServiceAccount route
POST /api/v1/internal/organizations/{id}/overage-stop and
cleared by .../overage-resume, both called by the
chargeback application. The organization-controller
returns the Organization to grow on its own once the
instant has passed.

owners.description:
Initial owner roster. Materialized as Keycloak group
members + UserAccess CRs by the organization-controller.

parentOrg.description:
Optional parent Organization slug — used for nested orgs
inside corporate Sovereigns (e.g. acme-pharmacy under
acme). Customer Orgs typically have no parent.

planSlug.description:
Purchased catalog plan slug (Workstream B, #4292). The
SINGLE truth-source for the resource cap the
organization-controller materializes on the boundary
namespace: the ResourceQuota + LimitRange (planQuota table —
S=2 vCPU/4 GiB purchased (the host-namespace quota adds the vCluster control-plane overhead on top), M=4/8, L=8/16, XL=16/32, Flexi=on-demand). The
plan SIZES the boundary and never selects it: every
Organization on every plan is backed by a dedicated
vCluster (founder 2026-09-10; the former free/S host-ns
tier gate is removed). Both CR-minting emitters resolve the
plan UUID to this slug before stamping the CR. Empty
defaults to "s" in the renderer.

slug.description:
Lowercase URL-safe identifier — used as the vCluster
name on the host cluster, the Keycloak group path, and
the Gitea Org name. Reserved values are rejected (the
list under not.enum): platform names, provider codes,
retired zone codes, environment types, and every
namespace of the bootstrap kit. Length 3-32.

sovereignRef.description:
FQDN of the Sovereign hosting this Organization
(e.g. omantel.omani.works). Authoritative once the
organization-controller (slice C1) reconciles.

suspendReason.description: Why the Organization is suspended; empty when it is not.

suspended.description:
Billing enforcement (products/chargeback DESIGN.md §9.7).
Set by the sovereign-admin API's operator-only
POST /api/v1/organizations/{slug}/suspend (cleared by
.../resume) when the chargeback application escalates
collections, a prepaid balance reaches zero, an operator
decides, or the external billing system commands it. The
organization-controller parks the per-Org Flux
reconciliation (spec.suspend on the per-Org
Kustomizations) and surfaces a Suspended condition. It is
never inferred: only the explicit route sets it.

tenantPublic.description:
Optional per-Org public-hostname binding. When set
the organization-controller renders a Gateway-API
HTTPRoute in the Org's namespace pointing at the
supplied backend Service. Empty (zero value) means
"no public hostname" — the Org is reachable only
via the per-Sovereign console wildcard.

Motivating fix: issue #1629 follow-up. PowerDNS
now resolves `<slug>.<parentDomain>` for every
Org mapped onto a Sovereign's role=org-pool parent
domain, but without an HTTPRoute attached the
Cilium Gateway falls through to the marketplace
tenant-wildcard route and serves the storefront
landing page instead of the tenant's product.

backendPort.description:
Service port number to route to. Defaults to
80 when zero.

backendService.description:
Service name the HTTPRoute routes "/" to. MUST
resolve in the Org's host namespace (= slug).
Required when parentDomain is set; the
controller surfaces TenantRouteFailed if absent.

parentDomain.description:
Apex zone the per-tenant hostname lives under
(e.g. "omani.homes"). MUST be one of the
Sovereign's parent_domains entries — operators
validate at admission via the bootstrap-api.

product.description:
Operator-meaningful tag carried on the rendered
HTTPRoute labels (e.g. "wordpress", "nextcloud",
"gitlab"). Surfaced on the access-matrix UI for
per-product filtering. Optional.

subdomain.description:
Leftmost label of the per-tenant hostname.
Defaults to spec.slug when empty.

tier.description:
org = self-service signup, no DMZ, per-Org Keycloak realm.
corporate = managed onboarding, dedicated DMZ vCluster
auto-provisioned (EPIC-5 #1100), per-Sovereign realm
federation.

giteaOrg.description:
Gitea Org reconciliation summary. Per Naming §11.2,
every Application gets its own repo at
gitea.<location-code>.<sovereign-domain>/<org>/<app>.

iacBootstrap.description:
Per-Organization IaC repo bootstrap state (ADR-0009 /
G117.3 / W2.C3 — issue #2742). On first reconcile the
controller calls iacbootstrap.Bootstrap which provisions
the canonical `<slug>/iac` repo, a per-Org `<slug>-iac-bot`
robot user with write-collaborator scope, branch
protection on main requiring three named status checks
(kyverno-admission, cert-manager-precheck,
dns-conflict-precheck), and persists the robot's
plaintext token to OpenBao at
`kv/org/<slug>/iac-bot-token` (issue #2765).

lastError.description: Most recent failure message when state=Failed.

repoURL.description: Canonical HTTPS URL of the per-Org IaC repo.

state.description:
State machine. Disabled means the controller's
OpenBao + Gitea deps are not wired (older deployments
without G117.3 env vars).

perOrgRealm.description:
Per-Organization Keycloak realm provisioning state
(#3084 Part 2). Distinct from keycloakGroup above:
keycloakGroup is a GROUP inside the shared Sovereign
realm, whereas perOrgRealm is a dedicated realm NAMED
after the Org slug, giving Tier-3 per-Org SSO its own
isolation boundary (own broker IdP + app clients). The
organization-controller find-or-creates the realm via
the Keycloak admin API on Org provisioning and tears it
down (DELETE /admin/realms/<slug>) on Org delete via the
`orgs.openova.io/per-org-realm` finalizer.

lastError.description: Most recent failure message when state=Failed.

realmName.description: Provisioned realm name (== spec.slug on success).

state.description:
State machine. Disabled means the per-Org-realm
feature flag (CATALYST_PER_ORG_REALM_ENABLED) is off
for this controller deployment.

hostCluster.description: Name of the host cluster the vCluster lives on.
